title: Advancing Transmission Electron Microscopy with an Open Gas Cell and Sub-0.5Å Resolution
content: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) has significantly advanced in visualizing matter at the atomic level. Specifically, the spatial resolution has improved to the 50 pm level in both broad and focused beam modes, by implementing aberration-corrected electron optics, monochromatizing the electron source, and stabilizing lens systems. This advancement shifts imaging resolution from being instrument-limited resolution to being object-limited [1–3], and, in turn, enables single-atom sensitivity imaging across the Periodic Table of Elements and reconstruction of the three-dimensional atomic structure of nanostructured materials [4, 5]. However, relating such measurements to the nanomaterials’ functions and properties is challenging, because surfaces of most nanomaterials dynamically adapt to their environment. To address this challenge, we have developed open and closed gas cell reactors for confining reactive environments to the vicinity of the nanomaterials and applying them for in situ and operando atomic-resolution TEM of nanomaterials at high spatiotemporal resolution and under controlled environmental conditions. Thus, we can advance the understanding the role of gas-surface interactions in catalysis [6], crystal growth, and corrosion.
